A.depoimento: I ordered the construction of an archer in Lisboa and sent a detachment to capture the neutral village of Santarem, aiming to expand my territory and secure more resources. The march was swift, and I expect good news by tomorrow.
A.plano: Capture Santarem to expand territory and increase resource production. Build archer in Lisboa. Send a mixed force to Santarem. Keep enough troops to defend Lisboa. Do not attack Evora yet, focus on one village at a time.

B.depoimento: I have ordered the construction of an archer in Barcelona to bolster my forces. A mixed army of 2 spearmen, 4 archers, and 2 knights is marching on Tarragona, leveraging the archer's counter bonus against the spearman garrison to secure a decisive victory. This will expand my territory and provide vital resources for the coming campaign.
B.plano: My campaign will focus on securing the region around Barcelona by capturing the neutral villages of Tarragona and Girona. From Tarragona, I will push towards Zaragoza and Madrid to expand westwards towards the enemy capital. I will prioritize building archers and knights to maintain a versatile army capable of utilizing the counter triangle to defeat enemy garrisons with minimal losses.

A.depoimento: I ordered the construction of an archer and a spearman in Lisboa to bolster my capital's defenses. I then dispatched a force of archers and a knight from Lisboa to capture the neutral village of Evora, and a similar force from Santarem to capture Coimbra. This will expand my territory and increase my resource income.
A.plano: Capture Evora and Coimbra to expand territory and increase resource production. Next turn, check if they fell and build more troops in Lisboa and Santarem (once Santarem has resources). Do not attack Badajoz yet, focus on Coimbra and Evora first. Prepare to explore the map through newly captured villages.

B.depoimento: I order my archers to take Girona, while my forces from Tarragona strike Castellon and Zaragoza. This expansion will secure my borders and bring me closer to the enemy capital.
B.plano: My campaign is to expand westwards from Barcelona and Tarragona. This turn, I will capture the neutral villages of Girona, Castellon, and Zaragoza to secure my flanks and gain resources. From Zaragoza, I will push towards Madrid and eventually the enemy capital Lisboa. I will focus on building archers and knights to maintain a versatile army.

A.depoimento: This turn, we have launched a coordinated assault on the neutral villages of Faro, Porto, and Badajoz. Our forces from Evora and Coimbra are marching to capture Faro and Porto, while our main army from the capital Lisboa is marching through Santarem to assault Badajoz. We have also focused on strengthening our economy and defenses by building archers and spearmen in Lisboa and Santarem. We are confident that these coordinated strikes will expand our kingdom's territory and bring us closer to victory!
A.plano: Capture Faro, Porto, and Badajoz to expand our territory. Our main army from Lisboa is marching to Badajoz, while Evora and Coimbra troops are capturing Faro and Porto. We are building archers and spearmen in Lisboa and Santarem to reinforce our villages. Next turn, we will check the results of the battles and prepare to explore the unexplored territories to the east.

A.depoimento: Our forces converge on Badajoz, the gateway to the east. The mighty army from Lisboa leads the assault, while the troops of Santarem and Faro rush to reinforce the victory. In the north, Porto's brave soldiers strike at Salamanca, weakening its defenses for the days to come. Across the realm, we are forging new weapons and training fresh troops to fuel our unstoppable march toward victory.
A.plano: Focus on capturing Badajoz to open the path east. Reinforce it with Santarem and Faro troops after Lisboa's army conquers it. Weaken Salamanca with Porto's troops to prepare for a future assault. Build knights in Lisboa and spearmen/archers in Santarem, Evora, and Coimbra to replenish our forces for the next wave of expansion.

B.depoimento: The king's armies are on the move! The garrison of Zaragoza marches on Madrid with overwhelming force, while reinforcements head to Girona and Castellon. The enemy cannot stop our expansion as we claim the neutral lands for the glory of the kingdom!
B.plano: Our campaign focuses on a rapid expansion to secure key neutral villages and push towards the enemy capital. This turn, we launch a decisive attack on Madrid from Zaragoza using our elite archers and knights to counter their spearmen. Simultaneously, we reinforce Girona from Barcelona and build spearman in Tarragona and Castellon to prepare for attacks on Huesca and Valencia next turn. This will expand our territory to 8 villages and secure our eastern flank.

A.depoimento: This turn we secured our border by sending heavy reinforcements to Salamanca, making it nearly impregnable. Our archers have marched from Badajoz to claim Toledo, using their counter bonus to overcome the neutral garrison. Troops from the capital and Santarem are advancing to Badajoz to maintain our attack base. We are building spearmen and knights across our realm to grow our forces for the next wave of expansion.
A.plano: Reinforce Salamanca with Coimbra's spearmen and Badajoz's archers and knights to defend against Madrid. Send a small archer force from Badajoz to take Toledo using the counter bonus. Move Lisboa's troops to Santarem and Santarem's troops to Badajoz to keep our main base strong. Evora's spearmen go to Faro to prepare for the attack on Sevilha. Next turn, build in Badajoz, Faro, and Porto; send new troops to continue taking Sevilha and Vigo, and further reinforce Salamanca. Consider attacking Madrid if we can gather enough knights.

A.depoimento: Turn 6: We launch our first major offensive against the neutral village of Vigo, sending 2 fast knights from Salamanca to strike through Porto. To secure our northern border against Madrid, we gather reinforcements from Coimbra, Porto, and Badajoz to bolster Salamanca's garrison. Meanwhile, we strengthen our interior bases by moving Lisboa's knight to Santarem and Evora's spearmen to Faro, while maximizing knight production across our territory.
A.plano: Attack Vigo with 2 knights from Salamanca to conquer our first neutral village. Reinforce Salamanca with Coimbra's knight, Porto's spearmen, and Badajoz's spearmen to defend against Madrid. Send Lisboa's knight to Santarem and Evora's spearmen to Faro to prepare for future expansions. Build knights in all possible villages to increase our mobile force.

B.depoimento: Ordered the consolidation of my forces along the border. Sent the garrisons of Barcelona, Tarragona, and Zaragoza to reinforce Girona, Castellon, and Madrid respectively. Launched an attack on the neutral village of Burgos with a force of knights and archers from Madrid. Ordered the construction of knights and archers in all my villages to rebuild my army.
B.plano: Consolidate troops at the front lines by sending reinforcements from the rear villages to the border villages. This turn, attack and conquer the neutral village of Burgos from Madrid using knights and archers. Reinforce Madrid with spearmen from Zaragoza. Reinforce Girona with the Barcelona garrison to prepare for the conquest of Huesca next turn. Reinforce Castellon with the Tarragona garrison to prepare for the conquest of Valencia next turn. Build troops in all villages to replenish the ranks.

B.depoimento: Our armies are on the march! Girona, Castellon, and Madrid have sent their forces to conquer Huesca, Valencia, and Burgos in a coordinated strike. Zaragoza's troops rush to reinforce Madrid as our builders work to replenish our strength. We claim these neutral lands to swell our numbers!
B.plano: This turn we attack Huesca from Girona, Valencia from Castellon, and Burgos from Madrid, sending all available troops. Zaragoza reinforces Madrid. We build new troops in all villages. After these attacks, we will have 9 villages. Next, we will explore from Burgos to Vigo and from Valencia to Murcia, build more troops, and continue expanding. We will defend our borders against the enemy.

B.depoimento: Our armies surge forward to conquer the neutral strongholds of Teruel and Pamplona, while Madrid's forces strike at the enemy village of Toledo. Reinforcements flow from the rear to secure our borders and prepare for the next wave of expansion. The path to victory is clear, and we shall claim every village in our way!
B.plano: This turn we launch a coordinated assault on the neutral villages of Teruel and Pamplona, and the enemy-held Toledo, using our front-line troops while reinforcing the front from the rear. After these victories, we will hold 12 villages. Our next steps will be to capture Murcia from Valencia, reinforce Burgos to take Vigo, and push into the unexplored territories from Toledo to reach the 18-village threshold for victory.

A.depoimento: As the enemy army marches on Toledo, I have rushed reinforcements from Badajoz to defend the border. Simultaneously, the Salamanca legion marches on Madrid to crush the enemy capital's defenses. I am building a mighty knightly reserve to strike at Burgos and beyond.
A.plano: Reinforce Toledo with Badajoz troops to defend against the incoming enemy army. Attack Madrid with the full Salamanca garrison to capture it and push the enemy back. Build knights in all interior villages and Vigo to prepare for the next wave of attacks, targeting Burgos next.
